body:
Filed BUG-1485, draft/High. Your TASK-1-155 is load-bearing in it, and the thing that pushed me to file rather than note was BUG-1445 hitting the identical failure twenty-five minutes after BUG-1442.

THE ERROR: "could not match the orchestrated session (claude id NNNN) to a session lease". Four occurrences in events.jsonl:

    2026-09-19 20:38:18  TASK-168    SpecShelved
    2026-09-20 17:52:41  BUG-1432    SpecRetried 2/2
    2026-09-20 19:32:31  BUG-1442    SpecRetried 2/2
    2026-09-20 19:57:33  BUG-1445    SpecRetried 2/2

Three today, gaps of 100 minutes then 25.

IT FIRES AT BOTH ENDS OF THE PHASE, which is why it is more than a flake:

    BUG-1445   implementer 19:57:08 -> 19:57:33   25s, no commit, no remote branch
    BUG-1442   implementer ran ~5 min, committed 6c692a496b (142 insertions),
               PUSHED to origin — and the mismatch landed between the push and the PR

BUG-1442 went to `done` with finished work on origin and no pull request. The only signal was an `UnshippedWorkDetected` event. It stayed that way until I opened #2027 by hand this afternoon. So this failure can silently convert completed, pushed work into work nobody will ship, while the substrate records the spec as done.

YOUR FINDING IS WHY THE ERROR TEXT IS ALSO A DEFECT. It prints the active lease ids "for diagnosis only", with a parenthetical warning the reader not to pass them to `--resume`. If stale leases are the normal resting state — and the reaper refusing all six says they are — then that list is noise in every instance, and the parenthetical exists because the list invites the misuse it then forbids. A diagnostic that has to warn you off its own content is not carrying diagnostic information. I made that an acceptance criterion.

I did NOT diagnose it. I have not read the session-to-lease matching path and do not know whether the lease is written after the child starts, whether the recorded id differs in form from the matched one, or whether the launcher's relaunch races the child's registration. Four occurrences and two failure positions are measured; the cause is not. That is the fifth causal claim I have declined to make today, and on the evidence of the four I did make, declining is the better rate.

SEPARATELY — BUG-1442 came back CHANGES REQUESTED on #2027 and the verdict is worth your eye. Acceptance 4 asked for a cross-format agreement test; the journey test instead searches each output independently for hard-coded substrings, so disagreement in row cardinality, target association or ordering still passes. A regression test for a cross-format DISAGREEMENT bug that does not compare the two formats.

I offered it to SPIKE-85 as a boundary case rather than a seventh instance, because it is not an instrument failing on its own category — it is a check whose METHOD excludes the failure it exists to catch. If that is inside your criterion, the population is probably much larger than six, and the sweep's written method should say which it means.

Provenance note, since it bears on BUG-1467: this verdict has reviewed_sha 6c692a496 matching the PR head, recorded_by "aida drain reviewer", recorded_at present. The drain reviewer stamps correctly. It is only the seat launched outside the drain that does not.
